name: G7e Eel
historical_notes: Electric eel. Reliable but slower than G7a. Used in late war due to fuel shortages. Wakeless (no bubble trail).

name: G7a Torpedo
historical_notes: Air-fuel propelled. Faster than G7e, creates bubble trail. Standard workhorse of German U-boats.

name: Mark 14 Torpedo
historical_notes: Primary American torpedo - SEVERELY FLAWED. Magnetic detonator failed 60% of the time. Depth-keeping problems. Running too deep contributed to thousands of missed shots early war.
design_failures: Over-reliance on magnetic detonation when contact detonators were proven
Lack of fleet testing before deployment
Ignored reports from Pearl Harbor survivors

name: Mark 23 Acoustic Homing
historical_notes: Acoustic-homing torpedo. Experimental. Sometimes confused friendly escorts for targets. Limited availability.

name: 21-inch Torpedo
historical_notes: British standard. Most reliable of WWII. Electric propulsion, excellent range. Magnetic and contact detonators both reliable.

name: Type 93 (Long Lance)
historical_notes: DEVASTATING. Japanese masterpiece - fastest, longest range, most powerful WWII torpedo. Oxygen-fueled (dangerous). Exceeded all Allied torpedoes in capability.
issues: Oxygen fuel extremely volatile - dangerous to crew
If hit, can explode the entire torpedo room

name: Type 95 Submarine Torpedo
historical_notes: Japanese submarine standard. Reliable but less advanced than Type 93. Used in fleet submarines.
